Stronger opposite-sign event distance from the endpoint product price
===================================================================

Retain the hypotheses and notation of SIGNED_ENDPOINT_PRICE.txt. In
particular A,B are actual nonnegative physical support endpoints, m>0,
m<=mu, and 6*m*A*B>=P>0 for the same law. Then

 (A+B)^2 >= 4*A*B >= 2*P/(3*m) >= 2*P/(3*mu).

The first inequality is the identity (A+B)^2-4AB=(A-B)^2>=0; the two later
inequalities use only the proved product price and positive mu. Thus a
directed square-root lower bound on 2*P/(3*mu) is an acquired lower bound
for the actual distance between the negative and positive support classes.
Every pair in the existing opposite-sign HIGH event has at least this
distance. The same event probability and conditional squared-distance upper
bound may be retained; all HIGH parameter and monotonicity gates must be
checked for the selected candidate as usual.

In INITIAL one may replace its old gap2 by
 max(old_gap2, 2*P/(3*mu)),
where P=max((SL-1)*rho_lower,SL*rho_lower-gamma_upper)-D_upper.
If separately acquired endpoint floors are available, their squared sum is
another valid lower bound to include in that maximum. No independent law
or separately spent defect budget is introduced.

Even the unsigned P0=(SL-1)*rho_lower-D_upper improves on the old expression
gap2=P0/((SL-1)*mu), because SL>5/2 gives2/3>1/(SL-1). This comparison
assumes P0>0, which is precisely the retained old positive-gap gate.
Using the stronger signed P can improve the distance further.

For a resource initialization which only uses m<=1/2, the valid new distance
is sqrt_lower(4*P/3). It may replace or be maximized with the former lower
gap bound in the positive-gap joint displacement estimate. Later updates
can use their acquired tighter mu and endpoints. The old positive-gap gate,
same-law inputs and all divisions/phase/moment checks are retained.

This is an analytic corollary, not a numerical INITIAL/resource certificate.
It never uses the rejected beta-based price. Exact accepted applications
must bind this note and the valid signed-price note with their sources.
